proposal.utterance: What BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation'?

entities.label: NormativeForce
entities.rationale: Normative force is the capacity or power of an obligation to bind, direct, or compel action. It is internally grounded in the bearer (the obligation or the obligated agent) and is dispositional rather than fully occurrent — it may or may not be realized in actual compliance behavior. This fits BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than Quality (which would be a static measurable property) or Role (which is externally conferred). It is distinct from the obligation itself (modeled as working:LegalObligation, a Role/SDC) — normative force is the disposition that inheres in the bearer of the obligation and is realized in processes of compliance, enforcement, or acknowledgment.

relations.rationale: NormativeForce is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016) as it is an internally grounded realizable entity inhering in an obligated agent or obligation-bearer.

Disposition is a subclass of Realizable entity (BFO_0000017); asserting this explicitly clarifies the chain BFO_0000016 -> BFO_0000017 -> BFO_0000020 as inherited, but the direct parent suffices. This relation may be omitted if the reasoner derives it.

open_questions: Should NormativeForce be treated as a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation (which is typed as BFO_0000023 Role) rather than a separate class, i.e., is normative force a disposition that inheres in the bearer of a LegalObligation rather than in the obligation itself?

Is the normative force in question specifically legal (arising from positive legal sources) or moral/deontic more broadly? This affects whether it should be a subclass of a more specific legal disposition or kept general.
Should NormativeForce be realized in working:BehavioralLegalManifestation (an existing Process subclass), which would make that relation explicit?
proposal.rationale_summary: The normative force of an obligation is best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) in BFO 2020. A disposition is a specifically dependent continuant that is internally grounded in its bearer and is realized (or fails to be realized) in processes. Normative force is precisely this: a binding capacity that inheres in an obligated agent (or in the obligation qua social object) and is realized in processes such as compliance, enforcement, or acknowledgment. It is not a Quality (BFO_0000019) because it is not a static measurable magnitude but a capacity for directed action. It is not a Role (BFO_0000023) because roles are externally conferred social positions, whereas normative force is an intrinsic binding power. The existing working:LegalObligation class is already typed as a Role (BFO_0000023), capturing the social-relational aspect of the obligation; NormativeForce as a Disposition captures the distinct binding-power dimension. A new class working:NormativeForce rdfs:subClassOf BFO_0000016 is proposed, with open questions about its exact bearer and realization targets.
